name.zh: Pinna 侏罗纪江珧化石壳

primary_specimen: VTT001-7, Paléontologie A16 / Jurassica collection, Switzerland

context.locality: Vâ Tche Tchâ near Courtedoux, Switzerland

scope: Original low-poly reconstruction of shell form based mainly on VTT001-7 as reconstructed in Koppka2018 Text-fig4 and photographed Plate1 J-L. Reconstructed missing pointed end is an interpretation, not an exact preserved scan.

scale.basis: Paper p29 table VTT001-7 H=3.2cm, L=(11.9)cm, I=0.98cm; p27defines I as single-valve inflation. Thus nominal two-valve thickness about2I=19.6mm.
scale.uncertainty: L is author-estimated from incomplete fossil, explicitly parenthesized. Thickness approximation assumes paired inflation; asymmetry is simplified. Not exact specimen geometry.

required_features: Long narrow lanceolate wedge, pointed anterior end expanding toward a broad rounded/truncate posterior edge; maximum width much less than length.
Two opposed moderately inflated valves with longitudinal meeting seam; not a flat leaf, solid spike or scallop fan.
Each valve has strong longitudinal median keel separating dorsal and ventral areas; cross section evolves from near-round at pointed end to rhomboidal/lanceolate toward posterior.
Nearly straight dorsal margin and gently convex ventral margin, anterior opening angle about25degrees; broad end should not flare into a wide fan.
Narrow byssal gape on anteroventral meeting edge, as indicated by Fig4B and Plate1B. Use small anatomically placed opening, not giant clamshell separation.
Weak radial ridges on dorsal half, roughly8 simplified at adult end; anterior comparatively smooth. Subtle curved growth lines on ventral half; no modern Pinna rudis spikes.
simplifications: Reconstruct pointed end as author Fig4, explicitly missing in actual VTT001-7; no claim of complete preservation.
Omit fine microscopic prismatic structure, many growth lines, fractures, sediment matrix, soft animal, byssal threads, and hidden muscle scars.
Artistic muted stone/tan palette; no claim of original life colors, no photo textures or reused meshes.
Closed presentation with narrow seam and small byssal gape; no need to expose or invent full inner nacre anatomy.
acceptance_focus: Front lateral silhouette matches Fig4A with119:32 proportions, not an equilateral triangle.
Top and end views show paired valve volume and median keels, total thickness near19.6mm.
Meeting edges and byssal gape are actual geometry, no detached decorative stripe.
Default four final views only; use cheap gray previews to catch shape before final render.
